comment: Measuring financial protection and benefits for children (or other vulnerable groups) a bit more explicitly. While the draft recognises financial protection, the proposed monitoring framework could more clearly distinguish digital-system performance, formal insurance coverage and effective access to affordable care. A small set of illustrative indicators could track unmet healthcare needs, catastrophic or impoverishing health expenditure, and coverage gaps among children, disaggregated by household income, disability and geography, using household surveys alongside administrative data. Linking these findings to budget allocations and expenditure on services benefiting children would help demonstrate whether digitalization improves equitable public spending and informs corrective financing decisions.
